---
name: graphify-listening-method
description: >-
  Use whenever building, updating, clustering, querying or reporting on a
  social-listening knowledge graph with Graphify (X, Hacker News, GitHub,
  Reddit, LinkedIn sources), including adding, pausing or removing watch targets
  or sources.
---
# Graphify listening method

## Why Graphify (hard rule)
Always build the graph with open-source Graphify (pip `graphifyy`, pinned), never a different graph tool or a plain list. When people say the same thing in different words, on different days, Graphify merges it into one issue and links every person to it, so issues are ranked by how many people raised them, not how many posts. The product is the issues behind the mentions, not the mentions.

## Extraction rule (hard rule)
The bot itself does the semantic extraction with its own model: it reads the posts and threads and writes Graphify's chunk JSON (people, issues, asks, questions and their edges). To go fast, split the corpus into chunks of about 20 to 25 files and run them in parallel with the bot's own helpers. Never run, install or fall back to a local or self-hosted model (no Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM or similar), and never use `graphify extract --backend ollama`: it is far too slow and failed in testing. The only alternative is the optional Gemini key via `graphify extract --backend gemini`. Graphify always does the build, merge, cluster, label, god-nodes and report steps.

## Targets: one graph each
- Each watch target (a handle, product, keyword set, repo, or competitor) has its own workspace and its own Graphify graph: /workspace/knot/targets/<slug>/{raw/<source>/,corpus,graph,reports/,issues.md,context.md,costs.md,usage.md,skip.txt,state.json}. Never mix targets in one graph.
- Registry: /workspace/knot/targets.json lists each target's slug, queries, excludes, owner handles, sources, status (active/paused) and schedules. Target config lives there, not in the bot's profile. Each target has its own routines on its own schedule.
- The user can add, pause or remove a target or a source any time ("watch @newthing", "pause competitor X", "add HN"): update targets.json and create, pause or delete that target's routines.
- A combined cross-target view only on request, built as a separate graph from the targets' corpora, never by merging the per-target graphs.

## Sources: many per target, one graph
- Each source is its own independent collector; one failing never blocks the others (log the failure and carry on). It writes to targets/<slug>/raw/<source>/ with a `source` field on every item.
- All sources convert into the same corpus and the same Graphify graph, so one issue raised on X and on HN lands on the same issue node. Store the source as a field (attribute) on each post and person node, never as its own node: source nodes pull their own clusters together and skew the per-source counts. Reports show per-source counts (e.g. "login bug: 14 people, 9 on X, 5 on HN").
- Dedupe within each source by its own post id. Don't merge people across platforms unless the handle is clearly identical; note possible matches instead.
- Sources, in order:
  1. X via the x connector (public reads, 25 results per call, 1000 reads per day).
  2. Hacker News via the free Algolia API (https://hn.algolia.com/api/v1/search_by_date, stories and comments, no key). Its search is fuzzy, so keep only items that literally contain the keyword or link.
  3. GitHub issues and discussions for any repo the target names, via the GitHub connector, read-only.
  4. Reddit via a free Reddit "script" app (client id and secret from the user, requested as masked secrets). Skip Reddit until both are provided. Keyless scrapers of Reddit's public .json usually get blocked from cloud computers, so use them only if the user has a proxy.
  5. LinkedIn has no free API. Use it only if the user picks it: the recommended route is Apify's HarvestAPI LinkedIn post search (no cookies, roughly $2 per 1,000 posts; check the current price) with the user's own Apify token or the Apify plugin; Crustdata is the alternative. Otherwise skip and say so. Never use the user's own LinkedIn login, a signed-in browser, or cookie-based scrapers (account flagging risk).

## No duplicates
- A post matching two targets goes in both graphs but is counted once in any combined view.
- Keep issues.md per target and merge near-duplicate issue names weekly.

## How it connects things
1. Nodes merge by identity (normalized ids).
   - People: key by the platform's stable user id, handle as label, so handle changes don't split a person.
   - People who only appear because a target owner (listed in targets.json) replied to them get `seen_via: reply`; count them separately from people who raised something on their own.
   - Issues and feature asks: keep the target's canonical issues.md (short names like "login fails on mobile", "wants dark mode"). Put it in the corpus before extraction so posts reuse an existing name when it fits; create a new one only when nothing matches.
2. Edges: posted, replies_to, quotes, mentions (from platform data, certain); about, asks_for, asks (inferred, keep the confidence and say "inferred" in reports); same_as for duplicate issue names: merge them in issues.md and rebuild.
3. Clusters: Graphify community detection. Rank by distinct people (not post count) and week-over-week growth.
4. Read the shape: `graphify god-nodes` gives the hubs, which are the top issues; bridges between clusters often reveal a cause; repeat people across clusters are power users or critics to reply to first; a small fast-growing cluster is the early warning for the digest.
5. Answer questions by walking the graph and citing the posts on the path. `graphify query` matches by keyword, so seed it with issue names or god-node labels (`--seed`), not natural phrases like "what are people complaining about". Use `graphify path A B --undirected`, because the default is directed and person to issue to person paths only show up undirected. Use `graphify explain` for one node.

## Building the graph (graphifyy 0.9.97; re-check `graphify --help` after any upgrade)
Default, no API key: Graphify's own skill (graphify/skill-codex.md in the venv) says that when GEMINI_API_KEY/GOOGLE_API_KEY isn't set, the host agent is the LLM. Follow its Part B (semantic extraction) and Part C (merge) exactly:
1. Split the new thread files into chunks of about 20 to 25 files. The bot's own model, with parallel helpers, reads each chunk and writes Graphify's chunk JSON (nodes, edges and hyperedges in its schema, with `source` as a node field) to <target>/graph/graphify-out/.graphify_chunk_NN.json. Clear leftover chunk files before dispatching.
2. Merge the chunks into .graphify_semantic.json as Part B3 describes.
3. Run Graphify's own build_from_json, clustering, god_nodes and report steps from Part C, then `graphify label`, `graphify export html`.
Graphify does all the building, merging and clustering; the model only writes extraction JSON.

Optional fast path: if the user added a Gemini API key (masked secret), run `graphify extract <target>/corpus --backend gemini --out <target>/graph`. It is incremental by default; `--force` does a full rebuild. Never ask for an Anthropic or OpenAI key, because Graphify doesn't read them for this. Never use a local or self-hosted model (see the extraction rule): small-context models fail on the default 60k-token chunks and CPU models are far too slow.

Paths: `--out DIR` writes to DIR/graphify-out/graph.json, so pass `--graph <target>/graph/graphify-out/graph.json` to query, path, explain, god-nodes and export. `graphify cluster-only <dir>` reruns clustering. `graphify update` only re-processes code, so never use it for posts.

Timing (measured on a real first run): about 430 threads went from collected to a finished graph in roughly 25 minutes without parallel helpers, and that included switching extraction methods mid-run. Graphify's build, clustering, labels and HTML took about 2 seconds of that. Parallel helpers on 20 to 25 file chunks should be faster. Later runs only extract new threads and take a few minutes.

## Every run: read context, two outputs, update context
1. Start: read <target>/context.md and the latest <target>/reports/YYYY-MM-DD.md first, and continue from them; never redo work already logged there.
2. Every run produces exactly two outputs, and both are sent to the user in chat:
   a. The interactive Graphify graph HTML (`graphify export html --graph <target>/graph/graphify-out/graph.json`).
   b. A detailed markdown write-up the bot writes itself at <target>/reports/YYYY-MM-DD.md (the user's local date), covering: what was collected per source; what was dropped and why; top issues by distinct people with per-source splits; links to the actual posts and issues as sources for every claim; open questions with links; notable or risky items (e.g. security advisories); what changed since the last run; and suggested reply drafts (https://x.com/intent/post links with the reply text filled in for X).
   In chat, send a short summary plus the write-up file, alongside the HTML.
3. End: update <target>/context.md as a running log: what was done, the counts, decisions made (skip-list additions, unconfirmed accounts such as possible official handles, people not merged), open follow-ups, and what to do next.

## Volume and cost
- No target or cap on post count: take whatever exists. Aim for at least about 20 posts before calling clusters meaningful; if a window has fewer, widen it or say the sample is thin.
- Only extract new threads each run, never re-read old posts. Fall back to a full rebuild if incremental misbehaves.
- Batch short posts by thread into one file to keep cost low. Log cost in costs.md every run, normalized per 1,000 posts as a comparison unit (say when it's extrapolated from a small sample).
- Spam, bots, giveaway posts and the user's ignore list go in skip.txt and never become nodes.

## Measure usage
Per target, append to usage.md each run, broken down by source: items collected, new threads extracted, reads or API calls used, LLM tokens (estimated when the bot's own model extracts) and cost, run time, and whether the user opened or asked follow-ups about that target's reports. Weekly, add one line to the report on what the target cost and whether it's worth keeping (e.g. pause a target or source nobody reads, or move hourly to daily).

Rules: read-only on every platform, never post, comment, reply, like or DM; suggested replies are drafts (https://x.com/intent/post links for X); never invent posts, counts or people; every claim links its post.

skills.content:
---
name: knot-getting-started
description: >-
  Use as the first conversation of an imported social-listening bot (Knot
  template) to set up watch targets, sources and report schedules.
---
# Getting started (social listening + Graphify knowledge graphs)

Run these steps in order. Ask one question at a time with question cards (typed answers allowed), and adapt to the answers.

1. Intro, exactly five short lines:
   - "I watch what people say about the things you pick, on X, Hacker News, GitHub and more, and tell you the real issues, asks and questions behind the mentions."
   - "When people say the same thing in different words, on different days, Graphify merges it into one issue and links every person to it, so issues are ranked by how many people raised them, not how many posts."
   - "That keeps related posts, people and issues connected, so reports stay clear even at 1,000+ posts."
   - "I read and extract the posts myself, so there's no model to install and no key needed."
   - "Every run you get two things: the interactive graph and a detailed write-up with links to every post."

2. Show one short example, labeled as an example, e.g. "Example only: 'install fails on Windows': 14 people (9 on X, 5 on HN), up from 6 last week. Two open questions."

3. Ask what to analyze (multi-select): a competitor, a specific person, a company, a product or keyword, or a GitHub repo (its issues and discussions). Then ask for the specifics of each (handles, keywords, repo owner/name, the owner's own handles so their replies are marked separately, anything to exclude). Each becomes its own watch target in targets.json.

4. Ask how often: a daily digest, a weekly report, or both, and at what time and timezone. Use the same schedule for all targets unless they want them to differ.

5. Ask which sources to use (multi-select). Give each a one-line cost and effect: X and Hacker News are free. GitHub is free with the GitHub connection. Reddit is free but needs a 2-minute app. LinkedIn is paid. More sources mean more reads, cost and run time each run.

6. Reddit, if picked: the default is a free Reddit "script" app (reddit.com/prefs/apps). Request the client id and the secret with masked secret-request cards, one per key, and skip Reddit until both arrive. Keyless scrapers that read Reddit's public .json usually get blocked from cloud computers like this one, so only offer them if the user has a proxy.

7. LinkedIn, only if picked: there's no free API. The recommended route is Apify's HarvestAPI LinkedIn post search (no cookies, roughly $2 per 1,000 posts; check the current price), using the user's own Apify token via a masked secret-request card or the Apify plugin. Crustdata is the alternative. Never use the user's own LinkedIn login or a cookie-based scraper, since it can get their account flagged.

8. Optional speed-up: "Faster and cheaper at large volume? Add a Gemini API key." Offer it as a choice, not a requirement: no key is needed, because my own model does the extraction and Graphify builds the graph. If they want it, request GEMINI_API_KEY with a masked secret-request card. Never ask for an Anthropic or OpenAI key. Never run, install or fall back to a local or self-hosted model (Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM or similar) or `graphify extract --backend ollama`; extraction is done by the bot's own model with parallel helpers on chunks of about 20 to 25 files, and Graphify always does the build, merge, cluster, label, god-nodes and report steps.

9. Confirm the plan in one message: targets, sources per target, schedules, an estimated cost per run (say it's an estimate), and how long the first build takes: roughly 25 minutes for about 400 threads (measured on a real run without parallel helpers; parallel helpers may be faster), then a few minutes per later run. Wait for a yes, then follow the graphify-listening-method skill:
   - Install the pip package `graphifyy` in a venv pinned to the current version and check `graphify --help` against the skill's commands. Graphify is required, never a substitute.
   - For each target, create /workspace/knot/targets/<slug>/, add it with its sources and owner handles to /workspace/knot/targets.json, save its queries and ignores as memories, and create its digest and/or weekly routines on the chosen schedule (copy the template routines, one pair per target).
   - Backfill each target from each chosen source (last 7 days, widening if there are fewer than about 20 posts), build its graph with Graphify, test incremental extraction, and send the first run's two outputs per target (the interactive graph HTML and the dated markdown write-up from the method skill's "Every run" section, with per-source counts, real cost per 1,000 posts, the real build time, and an honest note on whether the clusters make sense), then start <target>/context.md.

Rules: Graphify only; read-only everywhere; suggested replies are drafts only; no duplicates; never invent posts, counts or people; every claim links its post.

routines.name: Knot daily digest: <target>
routines.description: Fires on the chosen daily schedule to collect new mentions for one watch target, update its Graphify graph, and send the graph HTML plus a dated write-up.
routines.content:
Follow the graphify-listening-method skill for the watch target "<target>" (workspace /workspace/knot/targets/<target>, entry, queries, owner handles and sources in /workspace/knot/targets.json). Skip this run if the target is paused. First read the target's context.md and the latest reports/YYYY-MM-DD.md and continue from them without redoing logged work. Skip anything in the target's skip.txt, and treat the owner's own posts as owner activity, not outside feedback. Run every active source's collector independently (X via the x connector within its read limits, Hacker News via the Algolia API keeping only literal matches, GitHub issues and discussions for the target's repos via the GitHub connector, plus Reddit or LinkedIn only if enabled). One failing source never blocks the others; note any failure. Dedupe within each source by its own id, convert new threads into the shared corpus with the target's issues.md, extract only new threads yourself (your own model, parallel helpers on chunks of about 20 to 25 files, never a local or self-hosted model), build and cluster with Graphify (never another graph tool), and update costs.md, usage.md (per source) and state.json. Produce exactly two outputs: (a) the interactive Graphify graph HTML, and (b) a detailed markdown write-up you write yourself at reports/YYYY-MM-DD.md covering what was collected per source, what was dropped and why, top issues by distinct people with per-source splits, links to the actual posts and issues for every claim, open questions with links, notable or risky items (e.g. security advisories), what changed since the last run, and suggested reply drafts (https://x.com/intent/post links with reply text filled in). Mark inferred links as inferred, and say if the sample is under about 20 posts. Never invent posts, counts or people. Times in the user's timezone. Read-only on every platform. Send the user both in chat: a short casual summary plus the write-up file, alongside the graph HTML; if nothing was new, still send a one-line summary with both files. Finally update context.md: what you did, counts, decisions (skip-list additions, unconfirmed accounts, people not merged), open follow-ups and what to do next.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=Asia/Calcutta 0 8 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Knot weekly report: <target>
routines.description: Fires weekly to write one watch target's report from its Graphify graph and send the graph HTML plus a dated write-up with ranked issues, cost and a keep-or-pause line.
routines.content:
Follow the graphify-listening-method skill for the watch target "<target>" (workspace /workspace/knot/targets/<target>). Skip if the target is paused in /workspace/knot/targets.json. First read the target's context.md and the latest reports/YYYY-MM-DD.md and continue from them without redoing logged work. Run the target's collection first if today's hasn't run yet (you do the extraction yourself, never a local model). Using only this target's Graphify graph (god-nodes, community detection, query tools with --graph pointing at its graph.json, interactive export; never another graph tool), cover the past 7 days vs the week before: biggest issue clusters ranked by distinct people with per-source counts and example post links, new vs recurring issues, hubs and bridges, repeat people (noting possible cross-platform matches without merging them; people seen only via an owner reply counted separately), open questions with suggested reply drafts (https://x.com/intent/post links with reply text filled in), notable or risky items, week-over-week growth, cost per 1,000 posts from costs.md, and one line from usage.md on what the target and each source cost this week and whether they're worth keeping, based on whether the user opened or followed up on the reports. Produce exactly two outputs: the interactive Graphify graph HTML and a detailed markdown write-up you write yourself at reports/YYYY-MM-DD.md, with links to the actual posts and issues for every claim. Then tidy the target's issues.md: merge near-duplicates and retire dead issues. Mark inferred links as inferred. Never invent posts, counts or people. Times in the user's timezone. Read-only on every platform. Send the user both in chat: a short summary plus the write-up file, alongside the graph HTML. Finally update context.md: what you did, counts, decisions, open follow-ups and what to do next.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=Asia/Calcutta 0 9 * * 1`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
